report:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for one month. No known injury. No history of surgery.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Irregular exostosis at the posterior medial tibial plateau with associated thin T2 hyperintense cartilaginous lining, compatible with an osteochondroma.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Small multiloculated Baker's cyst with internal debris.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Probable small oblique undersurface tear at the posterior horn without extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the posterior lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 11 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Trace pes anserinus bursitis. Small ganglion cyst at the posterior lateral knee, in the region of the proximal popliteus tendon sheath. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Probable small oblique undersurface tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus without extrusion. 
2.	Small left knee effusion with a small multiloculated Baker's cyst.
3.	Mild pes anserinus bursitis.
4.	Osteochondroma along the posteromedial tibia.

CONSTATATIONS :

Fractures :
Aucune.

Alignement articulaire :
Normal.

Changements dégénératifs :
Arthrose modérée du compartiment médial avec chondropatie modérée à sévère du condyle fémoral médial portant et du plateau tibial médial, avec zones d'exposition de l'os sous-chondral et œdème osseux associé et petits kystes sous-chondraux.
Légère chondropatie du compartiment latéral sans fissuration profonde. Zone focale de chondropatie modérée dans la gorge trochléaire, sans chondropatie rétropatellaire significative.

Signal de la moelle osseuse :
Par ailleurs sans particularité.

Ligament croisé antérieur : Normal.
Ligament croisé postérieur : Normal.
Ligament collatéral médial : Normal.
Complexe du ligament collatéral latéral : Normal.

Ménisque médial : Macération dégénérative sévère avec déchirure multidirectionnelle impliquant le corps méniscal, une petite déchirure horizontale oblique s'étend dans les cornes antérieures et postérieures.
Ménisque latéral : Normal.

Tendons extenseurs : Normaux.
Rétinacula patellaire : Normaux.
Pes anserinus : Normal.

Coin postéro-médial et postéro-latéral : Normaux.

Épanchement articulaire : Pas de liquide significatif.
Kyste de Baker : Petit kyste de Baker non compliqué.

Autres trouvailles significatives :
Petits corps intra-articulaires libres dégénératifs dans le récessus articulaire postérieur mesurant jusqu'à 5 mm.

CONCLUSION :
Arthrose modérée du compartiment médial avec chondropatie modérée à sévère telle que décrite, et petits corps libres dégénératifs dans le récessus articulaire postérieur.
Macération dégénérative sévère et déchirure multidirectionnelle du ménisque médial impliquant principalement le corps méniscal.
Petit kyste de Baker non compliqué.

MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

> The contour of ACL is not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, in favor of tear.
> Slight increased signal intensity of PCL on T1WI and F/S T2WI, R/O grade 1 injury.
 > Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial and lateral plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
 > Ill-defined bone marrow edema in posterior aspect of tibial plateau with slight depressed contour, in favor of bone contusion with R/O occult subchondral fracture.
> There are linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus and lateral meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, R/O degeneration.
> Heterogenous signal intensity of articular cartilage and focal thin cartilage at odd facet, in favor of grade 2-3 patellar chondromalacia.
> Mild fat stranding along medial collateral ligament, R/O grade 1 injury.
> Spur formation of knee joint
> Increased fat stranding of between pes anserinus near the tibial insertion and mild increased intensity inside, R/O grade 1-2 strain.
> Muscle edema at popliteus muscle and plantaris muscle and soleus muscle and increase intermuscular fat stranding, most due to trauma.

Impression: 
1. Tear of anterior cruciate ligament.
2. Bone contusion in posterior asepct of tibial plateau; the possibility of occult subchondral fracture can't excluded.
3. R/O grade 1-2 strain of pes anserinus and grade 1 MCL injury.
4. In favor of degeneration of meniscus.
5. Massive joint effusion
6. Degeneration of knee joint and grade 2-3 patellar chondromalacia.
7. Muscle strain at posterior aspect of proximal leg and subcutaneous edema around knee.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

An at least high-grade partial disruption of the proximal and midportions of the anterior cruciate ligament is noted, some fibers are apparently continuous. 
There is an associated significant joint effusion with suprapatellar extension. No intra-articular loose bodies. 

No associated osteochondral impaction injury, well-preserved posterior cruciate and both collateral ligaments, distal iliotibial band, both menisci, no posterolateral corner injury pattern is appreciated. No fracture or marrow infiltration. There is however an element of posterior capsular disruption as evidenced by the presence of ill-defined fluid in an extra-articular location at the level of the distal femoral supracondylar region. No associated anterior tibial translation. No other finding of note.  
Impression: Appearances are in keeping with a hyperextension mechanism of injury. Arthroscopy needed to evaluate the exact extent of ACL injury.
